sections.h2: Cocoa's New York record was 5.5 times the 2022 average, then prices unwound

chart.title: Prices peaked in December 2024 and fell back to a spring 2026 low near US$2,850
chart.sub: US$ per tonne, at the dates shown.
chart.source: ICCO daily price and market review; press reports; market data aggregators.

sections.means: High prices cut demand and the 2024/25 crop recovered, so the 2023/24 shortage of 494,000 tonnes had already turned into a small surplus.
sections.todo: Treat the 2026 price rebound as unconfirmed, since ICCO has temporarily withheld 2025/26 production and grindings data.

sections.h2: Madagascar's vanilla export price fell about 90% between 2019 and 2025

chart.title: The collapse followed a scrapped price floor in 2023, not a cyclone
chart.sub: Madagascar average export price, US$ per kg.
chart.source: UN Comtrade (unit value, this blog's calculation); Central Bank of Madagascar.

sections.means: Exports were held back by a minimum price that was scrapped in May 2023, and the unsold backlog then flooded the market.
sections.todo: Use the central bank series for current prices, since trade quotes for cured Grade A beans run several times higher than its US$38 average.

sections.h2: India's cocoa-bean import bill tripled in 2024 while tonnes rose 39%

chart.title: Cocoa-bean imports cost three times as much in 2024 on 39% more tonnes
chart.sub: Value of cocoa-bean imports, US$ million.

sections.means: Because the price is set in London and New York, an Indian chocolate maker pays the West African shortage price whatever the origin of its beans.
sections.todo: Plan any expansion of Indian cocoa around today's lower prices, since farm-gate prices have already fallen by about half.
